root_cause.text: In the Ceph filesystem, two code paths (ceph_finish_lookup() and ceph_lookup()) call d_add(dentry, NULL) on a negative dentry that is already hashed in the dcache, causing __d_rehash() to reinsert the same node into the hlist_bl bucket, corrupting the hash list (e.g., creating a self-loop) and leading to infinite loops in __d_lookup().
root_cause.evidence: The patch adds `if (d_unhashed(dentry))` guards before `d_add(dentry, NULL)` in both `fs/ceph/dir.c` locations, as shown in the diff. The commit message explicitly states that "d_add() goes through __d_add() to __d_rehash(), which unconditionally reinserts dentry->d_hash into the hlist_bl bucket. If the dentry is already hashed, reinserting the same node can corrupt the bucket, including creating a self-loop." The provided RCU stall trace demonstrates the resulting infinite walk in __d_lookup().

intent_record.intent_summary: Guard against calling d_add on an already hashed dentry to avoid kernel inconsistency.
intent_record.what: Added a condition check `if (d_unhashed(dentry))` before calling `d_add(dentry, NULL)`.
intent_record.how: The change ensures that `d_add` is only called if the dentry is not already in the hash table, preventing potential double-insertion or overwriting of a hashed dentry.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix a potential race where a negative dentry could overwrite an existing positive dentry in the ceph lookup path for complete directories.
intent_record.what: Added a conditional check `if (d_unhashed(dentry))` before calling `d_add(dentry, NULL)` in the ceph_lookup function.
intent_record.how: Previously, `d_add(dentry, NULL)` was called unconditionally when the directory was marked as complete and lookup resulted in -ENOENT. Now, the negative dentry is only added if the dentry is not already hashed, preventing the overwrite of an existing positive dentry.
